_readme: Per-category ML/physics spec for Moon <-> Earth analog scores. Read by notebooks/ssl_colab.ipynb. Expressions are Python evaluated over a table whose columns are the patch columns plus the resolved aliases below (helpers: log10, log1p, abs, clip, minimum, maximum, where, exp, sqrt, nan, nsum, nmean, contains). In labeling functions / impossible pairs, suffix _M = Moon patch, _E = Earth patch. A comparison with NaN is False, so a rule with missing data abstains. Feature names are unique across categories on purpose.

moon.rows_seen: 3609 = 3600 grid patches (10 km, polar stereographic, -76.3 to -89.8 deg) + 9 Artemis target rows (is_target=1, patch_id = config/targets.csv id)
moon.geology_catalog: data/catalogs/moon_geologic_units.csv (unit, name, unit_class_name, age, description, interpretation)

earth.rows_seen: 3877-4321 candidates (growing while env/terrain builds run): 30 named_site (patch_id = config/earth_sites.csv id), 192 impact_structure, 1099 volcano, 2556 landcover_sample (strata: bare_hot, ice_edge, bare_midlat, lichen_moss, sparse_hot, sparse_cold, bare_polar, ice_sheet, antarctic_ice_free)

data_contract.pixel_size_note: 10 km / 64 px = ~156 m on both bodies; slope scalars use a common 500 m baseline.

meaning.+1: Earth reproduces the Moon condition within the stated tolerance, for test purposes
meaning.-1: opposite / misleading: a test here would give the wrong answer for the Moon

score_semantics.band_rule: score >= 0.5 -> sufficient; 0 <= score < 0.5 -> partial; score < 0 -> avoid; NaN -> not_applicable / unknown

pair_score.raw: raw = alpha_ssl * z(cos(e_M, e_E)) + (1 - alpha_ssl) * z(kernel); z() = standardise with mean/std over random Moon-Earth pairs so the two terms share a scale
pair_score.kernel: kernel = 2*exp(-0.5 * mean_i(((x_M_i - x_E_i)/tau_i)^2)) - 1 over features present on both sides (needs >= min_feature_frac of them). Physical units, pooled across bodies, NOT per-body normalised. one_sided=earth_at_least_moon uses max(0, x_M - x_E). kernel=false features are LF/SSL inputs only. kernel = 0.5 at an average gap of ~0.76 tau and 0 at ~1.18 tau.
pair_score.score: score = min(cap_M (Moon-side hard_caps), cap_E (Earth-side earth_caps), score_cap, tanh(a * (raw - b)))

calibration.method: tanh_platt (2 parameters per category, a > 0 so the map is monotone)
calibration.prior: score = tanh(kernel): with raw in kernel z-units, a0 = std_k and b0 = -mean_k/std_k over random pairs. Used as-is when a category has fewer than min_anchors_to_fit anchors. Meaning: a pair is sufficient (>= 0.5) when its features lie within ~0.75 tau of each other on average; the tolerances tau are the stated physics assumptions.
calibration.optional_head: Prior-Labs/TabPFN-v2-reg on [z_cos, z_kernel, weak_vote, feature gaps] once a category has >= 30 reviewed anchors (check the model-card licence). Default stays tanh_platt.

image.fallback_backbone: facebook/dinov2-base (if VRAM allows) or timm resnet18 (if HF download fails)
image.why_not_sunvis: sunvis exists only for the Moon; a zero channel for Earth would let the encoder identify the body. Illumination is handled by its own category.
image.embedding: concat(CLS, mean patch tokens) = 768-d, pooled-mean centred, L2-normalised
image.loss: VICReg(sim=25, var=25, cov=1) on projector outputs + lambda_coral * CORAL(Moon vs Earth) on the 768-d representation

tabular.corruption: SCARF: 30% of features replaced by the same feature from a random patch of the same body, + N(0, 0.05)
tabular.inputs: category features standardised with POOLED (Moon+Earth) mean/std in physical units, NaN -> 0 plus a missing-indicator per feature

text.loss: MultipleNegativesRankingLoss on (Moon unit text, Earth positive, Earth hard negative) triplets mined with the lithology ontology

ssl.domain_checks: Report linear-probe Moon-vs-Earth AUC on held-out spatial blocks for every embedding. AUC > 0.9 means the embedding mostly encodes the body: lower alpha_ssl to 0.3 or fall back to the kernel.

spatial_cv.why: Neighbouring 10 km patches are strongly autocorrelated; random splits leak. SSL is trained on folds != holdout; invariance, domain AUC and kNN stability are reported on the holdout blocks.

flag_highland.note: every non-mare unit: all south-pole units sit in feldspathic highland crust (with SPA-related mafic admixture)

geology.name: Geology, mineralogy, surface materials

text: unit name + description + interpretation from data/catalogs/moon_geologic_units.csv
context (tags, GVP rock type and summary, impact-catalog row)

geology.lithology_kernel: k_lith = clip(sum_c w_c[M] * flag_c[E] / sum_c w_c[M] - sum penalties[E], -1, 1); penalties are not applied to impact structures for flag_aqueous_sed. Earth rows with no lithology text and no class hit get NaN (unknown), not a made-up score.

labeling_functions.why: mare = basalt (rare at the south pole)
carbonates, evaporites, clays, sandstone need liquid water; absent on the Moon
ice sheet / glacier surface: no rock to test on
evolved silicic rocks are very rare on the Moon

mandatory_caveats: No Earth rock is space-weathered (no nanophase iron, agglutinates, solar-wind implantation); spectra and grain surfaces differ.
Terrestrial anorthosites carry more sodic plagioclase than lunar ferroan anorthosite; Earth rocks also carry hydrous alteration and weathering rinds.
Macrostrat units are map-scale (km); the lithology at the exact test spot must be checked in the field.
South-pole Moon units are all highland/crater materials, so Moon-side geology varies little across patches.

terrain.name: Terrain / topography
terrain.status: learned (DEM image SSL + scalar SSL) + kernel

labeling_functions.why: relief within x1.4, mean slope within 3 deg, steep share within 15 pp
relief differs by more than x4
Copernicus GLO-30 is a surface model: canopy/buildings add false roughness, water is flattened

earth_caps.why: DSM canopy/buildings or water dominate the DEM

mandatory_caveats: Compared at a 500 m slope baseline and ~156 m pixels: boulders and craters below ~100 m (lander- and rover-scale hazards) are not resolved; check with LROC NAC-scale DEMs.
Gravity changes landforms: the simple-to-complex crater transition is ~15-20 km on the Moon vs ~2-4 km on Earth, and slope stability differs, so similar statistics can come from different landforms.
Earth relief is shaped by water, ice and wind and is often soil- or vegetation-covered; lunar relief is impact-dominated and regolith-mantled.
Copernicus GLO-30 is a surface model: canopy and buildings are in the elevations.

thermal_illumination.name: Temperature, illumination, extremes

model.why_no_ssl: 8 physical scalars with disjoint Moon/Earth temperature ranges: SSL would only re-learn a distance and cannot say how many kelvin is 'close enough'. Tolerances below + anchors decide that.

thermal_illumination.normalisation_rule: Absolute units, pooled. Do NOT per-body quantile-normalise temperature: every south-pole patch (26-210 K mean) is colder than every Earth surface, so the physically closest Earth site is always the coldest one; quantile matching would wrongly pair a 'warm' Moon patch with a median Earth site.

features.name: t_cold_k
features.note: Moon: Diviner GCP diurnal minimum (moon_patches_tmin.csv), fallback coldest annual-mean cell; Earth: coldest-month mean night LST

features.name: t_range_k
features.note: definitions differ between bodies; used only by the optional tabular encoder

labeling_functions.why: closest approach: Earth surface reaching <= -60 C for a cold Moon patch
Earth surface >= 47 C vs a cold Moon patch
sub-tropical noon sun; Moon south pole stays below ~15 deg

hard_caps.why: PSR-dominated patch: 25-110 K surfaces have no Earth counterpart (Earth surface minimum ~180 K)

mandatory_caveats: PSR surfaces sit at ~25-110 K; Earth's coldest surfaces (East Antarctic plateau) reach only ~180-190 K. Cryogenic behaviour must be tested in cryo-vacuum chambers.
Vacuum: heat moves by radiation and conduction only. Earth wind and air give the wrong heat-transfer mode.

Lunar south-pole sun stays within ~1.5 deg of the horizon (plus topography) with black, skylight-free shadows; Earth illumination is scattered by the atmosphere and the sun is never that low for long except near the poles.
Earth polar night is seasonal (months); lunar permanent shadow lasts geological time and partial shadow periods are set by topography.

water_ice.name: Water, ice, permafrost, resources

features.name: ice_1m_frac
features.note: one-sided: an Earth site with MORE ground ice than the Moon patch is not penalised. ESA CCI PFR; else the 0/1 permafrost_flag (CCI or POWER T2M < -2 C proxy); else a MAAT ramp (0 at -1 C, 1 at <= -7 C)

features.name: ice_depth_m
features.note: often missing on Earth; dropped pair-wise when NaN

features.name: surface_ice_frac
features.note: Moon value = where surface ice is thermally stable, not where it is confirmed; hence the loose tolerance

labeling_functions.why: ice-cemented ground within ~1 m on both
liquid-water dominated (precipitation ~>600 mm/yr or wet soils)
bulk glacier ice is not ice-bearing regolith

hard_caps.why: surface frost at < 110 K in vacuum (sublimation-controlled); no Earth counterpart

mandatory_caveats: Earth ground ice sits at ~250-273 K with liquid films, salts and microbes; lunar ice sits at ~25-110 K in vacuum, so strength, dielectric response and extraction physics differ.
In vacuum ice sublimates instead of melting.
LCROSS found water (~5.6 +/- 2.9 wt%) mixed with other volatiles (e.g. CO, CO2, NH3, H2S, CH3OH) at Cabeus; terrestrial permafrost has no such mix.
Earth permafrost fraction can fall back to an air-temperature proxy when the permafrost map is missing; check the source flag.

dust_regolith.name: Dust, regolith fines, surface processes (wind dropped)
dust_regolith.status: prototype kernel (no SSL: Moon side has no per-patch dust data)

moon.prototype_note: approximate Apollo-era regolith values (fraction < 50 um ~40-50 wt%, bulk density ~1.3-1.6 g/cm3 in the top ~30 cm, dry, no organics); team to verify against a lunar regolith reference

features.name: dust_moisture
features.unit: m3/m3 (AMSR2 reads ~0.03-0.08 even on dry desert)

labeling_functions.why: glassy basaltic tephra is the usual source of lunar simulants

mandatory_caveats: Lunar fines are space-weathered (agglutinates, glass, nanophase iron), sharp and angular, and charged by UV and solar-wind plasma; Earth dust is weathered, rounded and moist.
On the Moon dust moves by rocket plume ejecta, impacts and electrostatic effects, not wind; Earth outdoor dust tests are wind-driven.
Moon-side values are one constant prototype: this score ranks Earth sites, it does not resolve regolith differences between lunar patches.
SoilGrids is a modelled 250 m product with no data on ice sheets and bare rock.

biology_sterility.name: Biology / habitability (Earth-side sterility)

features.name: bio_ndvi
features.unit: NDVI above the ~0.1 bare-soil baseline; Antarctic NaN -> 0

features.name: veg_frac
earth: nsum(wc_frac_tree, wc_frac_shrub, wc_frac_grass, wc_frac_crop, wc_frac_moss_lichen, wc_frac_wetland, wc_frac_mangrove)
features.unit: fraction (WorldCover has no data south of 60 S: treated as unvegetated at 10 km scale)

features.name: no_liquid_days
features.note: LF input only: frost is not sterility (hyperarid warm deserts are among the most lifeless sites)

mandatory_caveats: No Earth surface is sterile: even the hyperarid Atacama core and the Dry Valleys host microbes and organics, so every field blank carries biology.
Stations and camps (e.g. Concordia) add human-borne contamination around the site.
The Moon has no liquid water, organics or biosphere; low NDVI on Earth is a proxy for low biomass, not for sterility.

caves_subsurface.name: Caves / subsurface (pits, lava tubes)
caves_subsurface.status: RULE ONLY - learned model dropped (1 Moon target, ~5 Earth examples)

moon.note: the pit (8.3N 33.2E) is outside the south-pole patch grid; south-pole patches get NaN

rules_first_match.why: known basaltic lava-tube caves, not under forest/woodland
basaltic volcanic field: tubes plausible, unconfirmed

mandatory_caveats: Lunar pits/tubes may be much larger than terrestrial tubes (low gravity allows wider stable roofs).
Earth caves are humid, hold biology and are shaped by water and roof collapse; lunar caves are dry, in vacuum, and shielded from radiation and micrometeoroids.
Only one Moon cave target exists in this dataset; this category is a lookup, not a model.

ops_landing_mobility.name: Landing, mobility, operations, construction (derived)
ops_landing_mobility.status: derived from other categories + hazard kernel

model.rule: raw = nan-aware weighted mean of the calibrated category scores and the hazard kernel; then tanh_platt calibration on ops anchors (prior = identity when anchors are few)

working_thresholds.note: planning assumptions, not mission requirements; the 500 m baseline understates local slopes

labeling_functions.why: both hazard-rich: good for hazard-avoidance tests

earth_caps.why: forest, fields, towns or water: obstacles and surfaces with no lunar counterpart

mandatory_caveats: 1/6 g changes traction, sinkage, plume ejecta and human workload; outdoor Earth tests need reduced-gravity or mass-scaled complements.
No GNSS, ~1.3 s one-way light time, and no direct-to-Earth line of sight behind south-pole terrain.
Remoteness/isolation is not scored here; use site metadata (isolation tag) for crew-isolation studies.
